summary: Humboldt County lookout station on Trinity Summit, staffed by 1931, with a cabin and barn built in 1932; FFLA lists it as gone and a 2026 Forest Service project shares its name.

facts.design: Lookout patrol cabin and a barn, completed October 1932
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; no source describes what remains at the summit
facts.agency: Forest Service (1932 clippings name Forest Service carpenters)

events.note: A lookout named Crouse was at the station on Trinity Summit in August 1931
Forest Service carpenters built a cabin and barn for the lookout patrolman, completed October 1932

evidence.supports: A lookout named Crouse was at Trinity Summit in August 1931 (August 2, 1931 item)
evidence.quote: Lookout Crouse of Trinity summit reports

evidence.supports: Carpenters left for the summit on October 2, 1932 to build a cabin and barn for the lookout patrolman
evidence.quote: where they will build a cabin and barn for the lookout-patrolman

evidence.supports: Barn and lookout patrol cabin completed by late October 1932 (October 31, 1932 item)
evidence.quote: where they completed a barn and lookout patrol cabin

evidence.supports: The carpenters were Forest Service employees
FFLA lists Trinity Summit in Humboldt County as gone
Six Rivers project named Trinity Summit Restoration Project, carried out with the Hoopa Valley Tribe
evidence.quote: The Trinity Summit Restoration Project is a collaboration between the Six Rivers National Forest and the Hoopa Valley Tribe

evidence.supports: Project location is east of the Hoopa Square

sources.title: Trinity Summit Restoration Project
sources.publisher: Six Rivers National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: The 2026 Six Rivers project page does not mention a lookout; the link between that project and the old station is a name match only and is not asserted in the story. Clippings are transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page (originals not checked). One clipping spells the carpenter's name Wyllie and another Wylie, so names are left out. No construction date for the first station is in the sources; the 1931 staffing is the earliest evidence. Not in the cached firetower.org former-site list for California (matched on the name). An earlier draft named a site author; the cached page text does not name one, so the source no longer does.
